# CalibrateDS

> CalibrateDS is a set of local-first design system tools for design engineers who keep a design system in Figma and ship it in code. It treats the Figma file as source code and makes design drift measurable. It has three independent tools, each installed separately: PTB (`@calibrate-ds/cli`) generates components and tracks freshness, DNA (`@calibrate-ds/dna`) governs conformance, and a Figma plugin audits designs. Built by Deep Adalja.

## Naming

- PTB stands for "prompt to both".
- DNA is a name, not an acronym.

## PTB (`@calibrate-ds/cli`, command `ptb`)

PTB scans a Figma file, normalises it into a DesignSystemModel, and generates typed React + TypeScript components (CSS Modules) and `--ptb-*` CSS custom property tokens. Generated code is plain code the team owns.

- `ptb scan` writes the model to `.ptb/latest.json` and per-component context files to `.ptb/context/`
- `ptb generate-components` and `ptb generate-tokens` produce components and tokens
- `ptb status` shows Design, Code and Visual freshness per component; `ptb stamp` marks a component implemented
- `ptb verify` screenshots the component in Storybook and scores it against Figma; 0.90 or above passes
- `ptb dev` runs a Vite playground with variant controls sourced from Figma
- MCP server with 23 tools, the primary way to use PTB; `ptb mcp setup` configures Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VS Code

Install (Node.js 20 or later):

```bash
npm install -g @calibrate-ds/cli
ptb init
```

## How design freshness works

On every `ptb scan`, PTB computes a `designHash` per component and stores it in `ptb.lock`. `ptb stamp` copies that hash into `stampedHash`. If `stampedHash` equals `designHash` the component is ready; if they differ, Figma changed since the last stamp and the component is stale; if `stampedHash` is missing, it is not implemented. Generated files carry a `contextHash` in their header, which `ptb status` uses for the Code column. `ptb ci setup` writes a GitHub Actions workflow running `ptb status --fail-on-stale`; it reads only the committed `ptb.lock`, so CI needs no Figma token.

## DNA (`@calibrate-ds/dna`, command `dna`)

DNA is the governance tool: it checks that code keeps to the design system. It does not depend on PTB.

- `dna start` extracts the codebase's existing design identity (palette with primitive and semantic tiers, type scale, spacing grid) into `.dna/identity.yaml`, with per-rule provenance (`figma`, `code` or `hand`, and when). If it finds nothing, it writes nothing.
- `dna check` runs conformance in four layers: source lint, a cn-merge guard, rendered checks in headless Chrome, and structural manifests. Each run reports pass, nothing-to-check, or fail, and exits non-zero on violations, so it can gate CI.
- `dna allow` adopts a deliberate exception with a required reason. Exceptions and authority flips are appended to the decisions ledger, `.dna/decisions.jsonl`.
- `dna hook install` adds a git pre-commit hook that runs `dna check` and blocks failing commits.
- `dna similar` flags rebuilds and clones of existing components (advisory).
- `dna mcp` starts DNA's own MCP server, separate from PTB's, with five detector-only tools (`dna_check`, `dna_resolve`, `dna_inventory`, `dna_similar`, `dna_start_preview`) that never write source.

Install (Node.js 18.17 or later):

```bash
npm install -g @calibrate-ds/dna
dna start
dna check
```

With npx, use the full package name: `npx @calibrate-ds/dna check`.

## Figma plugin

Six modules: Accessibility Advisor, Component Readiness, Token Inspector, State Diff Engine, Stress Test (AI) and Token Exporter / Importer. Free on Figma Community. Runs locally, no account required.

## License

Both npm packages are licensed FSL-1.1-MIT. CalibrateDS is not open source; the source repositories are private.
